## MIDI File Preview (MF)

The MIDI family's renderer — and the one that most needed a design decision, because **a MIDI file has no sound**.

A Standard MIDI File is symbolic performance data: which notes to play and when. There is no audio until a synthesizer renders it, and no browser plays one from an `<audio>` element.

### So it draws neither a player nor a waveform

Unlike `AudioPreview`, this presents **what the sequence is**:

- a **pitch band** — the piano's full span, with the piece's own range shaded across it
- tracks, notes, running time, tempo, key, meter
- the **General MIDI voices** the programs name

### `program 40` → `Violin`

The GM Level 1 sound set is mapped, so a bare program number becomes an instrument name. That mapping is the difference between a debug dump and a preview someone can read.

### Everything shown is already a field

Every value comes from `MidiMetadataField`, populated by the extract pass. This stays a **view of extracted data and never a re-parse** — which is why it costs nothing in a collection.


Projected into the four format shells by `FilePreviewStage`, which owns the loading, failure and staleness panes — this component draws content only.
